name: MonarchSkipLink
title: SkipLink
wrapsNative: Button with MonarchButtonStyle that sets an AccessibilityFocusState binding; @FocusState and the accessibilityVoiceOverEnabled and accessibilitySwitchControlEnabled environment values decide when it is drawn
summary: A "Skip to main content" control at the top of a screen with many elements before the main part; activating it moves VoiceOver focus to the target through AccessibilityFocusState.
whenToUse: On a screen where a long toolbar, a filter row or a carousel stands before the content people came for, so VoiceOver and Switch Control users can jump past it.
whenNotToUse: On most screens: VoiceOver moves by heading and by container, and the navigation and tab bars are separate regions. Give section titles the header trait first.
api: init(_ title: String? = nil, target: AccessibilityFocusState<Bool>.Binding, isAlwaysVisible: Bool = false)

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in title "Skip to main content", for example "Skip to search".

options.name: target
options.description: The accessibility focus of the element to move to.

options.name: isAlwaysVisible
options.description: Draws the control for everyone, not only while an assistive technology runs or it has keyboard focus.

states.name: hidden
states.description: Without VoiceOver, Switch Control or keyboard focus it takes no space and is not drawn.

states.name: shown
states.description: A small secondary button with a down-to-line arrow and the title.

appearance: A small secondary MonarchButton with the arrow.down.to.line symbol. Colours come from theme roles in every theme.
platformNotes: On the web the link appears in the top corner when it is focused with Tab and moves focus to an element by id. On iOS it is drawn while VoiceOver or Switch Control runs, or while it has keyboard focus (Full Keyboard Access), or always with isAlwaysVisible; activating it sets the target's AccessibilityFocusState, which moves VoiceOver to the target. Android does not ship this component.
accessibility: A button named "Skip to main content" (or title) with a 44-point touch target.
Activating it sets the target's accessibility focus, so VoiceOver reads the target next.
It stays in the accessibility tree while it is not drawn, so VoiceOver can reach it.
edgeCases: The target must use .accessibilityFocused with the same binding.
Keyboard focus moves only with Full Keyboard Access; AccessibilityFocusState moves VoiceOver focus.

examples.title: Skip to the main content
examples.code:
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {
    MonarchSkipLink(target: $isMainFocused, isAlwaysVisible: true)
    Text("Main content starts here.")
        .monarchTextStyle(.body)
        .accessibilityFocused($isMainFocused)
}
.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)

examples.title: Custom target and label
examples.setup:
@AccessibilityFocusState private var isSearchFocused: Bool
@State private var query = ""

parityExceptions.reason: The web example is a hidden link that appears on keyboard focus, with an instruction to press Tab; iOS has no Tab order to show.
parityExceptions.convention: The iOS example shows the control drawn, moving VoiceOver focus to the same main content text.
